def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 → Def2 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    Def5 𝓑 F →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (F φ 🡒 K φ)) →
    ∃ ψ, 𝓢 ⊢ K ψ ⋏ K (∼F ψ)

translation: Target is the following proposition. For every choice of types Fm, S₀, and S, of implication, conjunction, disjunction, negation, truth, and falsehood on Fm, and of provability relations for systems of types S₀ and S on Fm, take any 𝓑 : S₀ and 𝓢 : S such that each proves every classical propositional tautology and is closed under modus ponens. For every pair of functions K, F : Fm → Fm, suppose that (1) for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ then 𝓑 proves K(φ); (2) every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢; (3) for every φ and ψ, 𝓢 proves the sentence K(φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K(φ) 🡒 K(ψ)); (4) for every φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) 🡒 φ); (5) there exists a sentence θ such that 𝓑 proves the biconditional θ 🡘 ∼(F(θ)); and (6) for every φ, 𝓢 proves K(F(φ) 🡒 K(φ)). Then there exists a sentence ψ such that 𝓢 proves the conjunction K(ψ) ⋏ K(∼(F(ψ))). The conclusion does not require ψ to be the witness θ from (5), and the negation in its second conjunct is inside K. Neither system is assumed consistent. Condition (1) is required of 𝓑, not of 𝓢, and (4) requires the sentence with the outer K, not a proof of K(φ) 🡒 φ itself.

divergences.description: The target ranges over arbitrary sentence types and functions K and F. It does not require K to be the syntactic operator B of the quantified arithmetic language, or F φ to result from substituting the Gödel numeral of φ into a single one-free-variable formula.

The hypothesis 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 transfers theorems from an abstract base; it does not identify that base with Q or require its axioms. Distributivity and B(Bp → p) are required directly in 𝓢 rather than obtained from the intended background theory.

Def1 requires necessitation for every theorem of the chosen base, more than the particular boxed tautologies and elementary arithmetic and equality axioms singled out as needed for the argument. It does not require necessitation for every theorem of 𝓢.

Def5 makes the existence of a base-provable fixed point for this F an explicit hypothesis. In the source it follows from the fixed point theorem for each formula F of the specified kind, rather than being a separate condition to check.

judgement.summary: Within the declared abstraction, the target preserves both the case (ii) hypothesis and the conclusion, including the scope of B in B¬F[s]. It captures the implication using abstract proof conditions rather than stating the arithmetic theorem directly.
